en.title: Shang-Chi's Avengers: Doomsday Return Is 5 Years Too Late
en.summary: After a triumphant debut in 2021, Shang-Chi has been notably absent from the MCU. Now, Simu Liu's hero is set to return in Avengers: Doomsday, but fans argue this comeback should have happened much sooner.
en.body:
When **Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings** burst onto screens in 2021, it felt like a breath of fresh air. It was a vibrant, action-packed origin story that blended martial arts spectacle with genuine heart, introducing **Simu Liu** as a compelling new hero. The film’s post-credits scenes hinted at future adventures, with the organization known as the Ten Rings set to return. However, the focus wasn't immediately on Shang-Chi himself, leading to a period of absence that has felt *surprisingly* long for fans eager to see more of the Master of Kung Fu.

Now, after a five-year hiatus, **Shang-Chi** is finally slated to rejoin the fray in **Avengers: Doomsday**, arriving in theaters on December 18, 2026. While **Simu Liu** himself expressed his happiness with the timing, feeling that the character's journey will be properly paid off in the massive crossover, many fans and critics feel this return is long overdue. The **MCU** faced a significant crossroads after **Avengers: Endgame**, grappling with how to introduce new characters and storylines while maintaining audience engagement. Some argue that **Shang-Chi** represented a perfect opportunity to pivot and expand the universe with a fresh perspective, rather than waiting for a major ensemble film.

## A Missed Opportunity for Expansion

**Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings** was a critical and commercial success, particularly impressive given its release during a challenging period for the film industry. It offered a unique blend of cultural specificity and universal superhero appeal, proving that there was a strong appetite for new heroes and diverse storytelling within the **MCU**. The decision to hold Shang-Chi back for such an extended period, only to integrate him into the next major **Avengers** event, has led to a sense that Marvel missed a prime window to build momentum for the character. Instead of a steady stream of solo adventures or supporting roles that could have further developed his character and world, fans have been left waiting.

## The Fan Perspective

For many viewers, the appeal of **Shang-Chi** lay in its originality and its departure from some of the more formulaic elements that have emerged in the **MCU** since **Endgame**. The anticipation for his return in **Avengers: Doomsday** is high, but it's tinged with the question of what could have been. Would a **Shang-Chi** sequel have provided a much-needed boost to the franchise's trajectory? Could it have offered a bridge between the established heroes and the next generation? The excitement for his presence in **Doomsday**, particularly with mentions of a prominent set piece involving **Channing Tatum**'s Gambit, is undeniable, but it’s framed by the sentiment that this should have been the *latest* in a series of outings, not a grand, delayed re-introduction.

What's Next

**Avengers: Doomsday** is scheduled for release on December 18, 2026. Details regarding **Shang-Chi**'s specific role and the other characters who will feature prominently are still emerging, but his inclusion marks a significant moment for the character's future in the **MCU**.

content_raw: No one was really too worried when Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings broke from the usual MCU model by following its final post-credits scene not with “Shang-Chi will return,” but rather “The Ten Rings will return.” After all, the second post-credits scene showed Shang-Chi’s sister Xialing taking her father’s place as the new head of the terrorist organization, so it made thematic sense. And Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings was an enormously entertaining film, so surely Simu Liu would be back soon as the title character, right? Turns out, the answer is, “Wrong.” Shang-Chi has been missing from our screens since 2021, and will finally return in Avengers: Doomsday . According to Liu, the wait was worth it. “I was so stunned by the fan response to the first film … [and it] definitely set off some sort of expectation in my mind that the character journey would be paid off somehow,” he told Empire . “When Doomsday came around, I was like, ‘This feels right.'” Happy though we may be for Liu’s feelings about his character, we respectfully disagree. We should have had at least one Shang-Chi sequel before Doomsday . For those who have been following the steady onset of superhero fatigue, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a pleasing outlier. For most, fan interest peaked with Avengers: Endgame , which put a nice button on the shared universe experiment that we’ve all been enjoying. No, COVID did not help, nor did the decision to follow Spider-Man: Far From Home , the first MCU movie released after Endgame and proper hit, with the lackluster prequel Black Widow . But generally, MCU movies have felt more shoddy since 2019. Along with Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 , and the cameo-laden mega-hits Spider-Man: No Way Home and Deadpool & Wolverine , Shang-Chi is a rare, under-appreciated bright spot. Liu puts in a star-making performance as a West Coast slacker who reveals himself to be the Master of Kung Fu, forced back into action to confront his warlord father Wenwu, played by the legendary Tony Leung. While the movie does devolve into sludgy, stock MCU visuals in its final act, director Destin Daniel Cretton manages to bring enough Wuxia influences to make the film feel distinctive, giving the MCU its best action sequences. By the time Liu stood toe-to-toe with Ryan Gosling as a rival Ken in Barbie , it was clear that we should have had multiple Shang-Chi sequels in production. But that never happened. On one hand, we can see why. After Shang-Chi , Marvel moved Cretton to the big leagues, tasking him with directing the next two Avengers movies, The Kang Dynasty and Secret Wars . Presumably, Cretton would have taken Liu with him, making Shang-Chi a centerpiece of the latest incarnation of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes.
